text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Education Minister Mehmet Saglam aims to abolish university entrance examinations and use school results as the basis for deciding who will win places at university.
- A government ministry plans a law aimed at protecting the Turkish language and halting the rise in the use of foreign words. The law would require workplaces and products to have Turkish names.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan says everything possible will be done for entrepreneurs wanting to open factories across Turkey.
- The public's expectations of more openness in political life are to be disappointed by planned changes in regulations covering the immunity of parliamentary deputies from prosecution.
- The Foreign Ministry is disappointed by the results of the first year of a customs union between Turkey and the European Union.
- Many key economic indicators for 1996, such as inflation and the budget deficit, show the economy will need to be watched very carefully in 1997.
- One member of a drug smuggling gang in custody is revealed to be the chauffeur of a leading official in an anti-terror squad.
- The wastefulness of the state has reached a critical stage. The number of official cars and the petrol they use is of great expense to the country.
